Hi Sophie / Tom —

Thanks for the questions. High-level answers below and I attached a short integration guide + a prompt governance checklist for reference. Happy to deep-dive in the workshop.

1) SDK + Auth patterns
   - We support three common modes:
     a) API key with short TTL (recommended for server-side): keys can be rotated via your KMS. SDK has built-in token refresh using a tokenProvider interface.
     b) mTLS for VPC/private deployments (recommended for high-security flows).
     c) Mutual OAuth: for user-context calls where you want delegated scopes.
   - Example init (Node):
     const client = new RedwoodClient({ tokenProvider: myKmsProvider });
     // SDK auto-refreshes tokens using provider.getToken()

2) Routing & model pinning
   - You can set routing policies per route: latency_slo, cost_budget, region_preference. Each policy maps to a priority list of model variants (e.g., redwood-base-8q -> redwood-base-4q -> open-compat-8q).
   - On capacity shortfall, the router applies the next compatible variant automatically; requests are tagged with route.metadata so you can track fallbacks.

3) Structured output & tool calling
   - We recommend using the structured tool-calling API for actions (returning typed JSON). Enforce schema validation on the client side and at the edge to reduce prompt injection surface.
   - Example: system prompt that defines the JSON schema + an instruction to never execute system commands from model responses unless verified.

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern
   - Candidate generation: semantic search using embeddings (sparse+dense hybrid) -> kNN top-K -> reranker model that scores pairs.
   - Metrics: NDCG@10, MRR, and human-evaluated precision at 1. We can provide an evaluation harness.

5) Prompt governance (versioning & injection mitigation)
   - Versioning: treat system prompts as code artifacts. Put them in a repo with semantic versioning (v1.0.0), tag releases, and tie evals/benchmarks to each version. Use CI to run regression checks against a prompt test suite.
   - Injection mitigations: canonicalize input, whitelist allowed tools, normalize user content, and run a prompt-safety classifier before sending to model. For high-risk flows, use a deterministic policy layer that enforces schemas and denies ambiguous responses.
   - Red teaming: run quarterly automated red-team jobs plus an annual manual red-team. Track findings in a shared issue tracker and require a remediation SLA for critical findings.

Next steps:
  - I'll bring a 30-min technical deck to the workshop covering SDK snippets, routing examples, and a walk-through of the prompt-versioning CI job.
  - Proposed workshop times: Wed 3/4 2:00–3:00pm PT (works per Marissa) or Fri 3/6 10:00–11:00am PT.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_integration_guide.pdf, prompt_governance_checklist.md

Regards,
